conservative.read: This plan prioritizes capital preservation with a target of around 1.5% per month. It significantly reduces risk by cutting leveraged positions and lowering concentration. Expect lower potential gains but also a much smaller chance of large losses.

plan: Trim QQQI to 20% to manage concentration while keeping income.
Reduce leveraged ETFs (METU, SOXL, MUU, PLTU, SPAL, MSFU) to small positions.
Introduce XLF at 4% to diversify into financials.
This plan balances growth with risk reduction.
It aims for steady growth with moderate volatility.
A modest cash buffer will be maintained.
balanced.read: This balanced approach targets around 2.5% per month by blending broad market exposure with quality tech and reduced leverage. It aims for risk-first growth, keeping drawdowns manageable. Leverage is kept low, and diversification is improved.

plan: Trim QQQI to 20% to manage concentration.

aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets around 4% per month by maximizing leverage and concentrating on high-conviction (though leveraged) names. It accepts substantially higher risk, including amplified drawdowns and the effects of leveraged ETF decay. Strict stop discipline is crucial.

plan: Increase QQQI to 30% to maximize income generation.

income.read: This income-focused plan targets around 1% per month by prioritizing yield from QQQI and other income assets. It aims for low drawdowns and reliable distributions, not capital appreciation. While income is the goal, NAV can still decline in market downturns.
